title: persona enumerate probes the CLI own environment instead of asking the daemon, so the primary diagnostic disagrees with reality
description:
persona/src/main.rs:167-199 implements the enumerate subcommand by calling probe_sources() in the CLI process:

    let sources = probe_sources().await;
    for attestor in &sources { match attestor.enumerate().await { ... } }

It never connects to personad. Every attestor probe reads process-local state:
  • ssh.rs:262-267 and 317 read SSH_AUTH_SOCK
  • did_key.rs:391 reads PERSONA_DID_KEYS
  • oidc.rs:97 and gpg.rs:249 read HOME
  • gpg.rs:310-320 shells out to gpg with the callers keyring and agent

The CLI runs in an interactive shell; personad runs as a systemd user unit (persona/src/main.rs:37-52) whose environment is Environment=RUST_LOG=info and nothing else -- no SSH_AUTH_SOCK, no PERSONA_DID_KEYS, and a different (or absent) gpg-agent.

What goes wrong: `persona enumerate` lists sources the daemon cannot see, and omits ones it can. The user runs the diagnostic command, sees "ssh-agent | spiffe://ssh.local/key/... | iaa1", then runs `persona whoami` and gets "no identity" -- or gets a Tailscale identity they were not expecting because that is the only source the daemon actually found. There is no indication the two commands are reading different worlds.

Why this generates issue reports: enumerate is the first thing anyone runs when identity is missing, and it is the one command that structurally cannot reproduce the daemon view. Every such report will look like a daemon bug and cost a round trip to discover it is an environment mismatch. The same divergence makes the docs statement in `persona log` ("personad writes structured audit events", main.rs:489) the only way to see what the daemon really enumerated.

Fix direction: add an RPC (or reuse FetchJWTSVID metadata) so enumerate reports the daemon view, and keep the local probe only behind an explicit flag such as `--local`, labelled as such in the output.
